messages:
sophia: Quick intake — bringing up zephyr-7b on dev cluster. Can folks run a few quick sanity checks and paste outputs? Minimal checklist: 1) simple generation 2) tokenization/eos behavior 3) streaming + stop sequences 4) quick int8 quant smoke 5) 100-sample eval if the above looks okay. @matt @kevin @lia :eyes:

matt: On it. Pinging with the curl I'm using and a couple quick outputs.

```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://dev-api.redwood.internal/v1/generate \\  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $DEV_TOKEN' \\  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\  -d '{"model":"zephyr-7b","input":"What is 2+2?","max_tokens":10}'
```

matt: Output (raw):
```
4
```

matt: Good on arithmetic. Now an instruction->structured output case: prompt = "Return JSON {\"sum\": 2+2}" with stop sequence '}' and max_tokens 40. Expected exactly one JSON object. Got extra trailing text.

matt: Example:
```
{"sum":4}

Note: result computed correctly but extra newline+text appended
```

kevin: Hmm this smells like stop-token not being honored during streaming after quant step. Seen similar with other 7b quant runs when tokenizer EOS id mapping is off. Quick tests: try setting explicit eos_token_id in server config or include stop=['}'] at call site.

alex: On the quant side: I ran a tiny int8-dynamic amin test earlier — perf looks good but small regressions on tight formatting tasks. For now recommend running quant profile with these flags: `quant_type=llm.int8` + `reduce_range=false` + `use_fp32_residuals=true`. That combo cut perf hit in our MATH microbench to ~0.5% instead of ~0.8%.

lia: I'll queue the 100-sample eval once we confirm stop/eos behavior. Using the usual eval harness (eval-bot). Starting the job if we get green on stop tokens.

deploy-bot: Deployment completed: zephyr-7b.dev -> staging (image gf-2026-03-20-01) :white_check_mark:

eval-bot: Eval job queued: job_id=9876, samples=100, suite=smoke-formatting. Will post summary when finished.

matt: Also noticed streaming duplicates the first token in one run: output started with '###' twice on the first packet then correct. Could be a transient batching boundary. Example snippet from logs: 
```
[stream] packet1: "###"
[stream] packet2: "### Hello, here's the answer"
```

kevin: If batching boundary causes duplicated prefixes, try disabling continuous batching for the endpoint (dev-only) or set max_batch_delay_ms lower to see if it reproduces. Also check tokenizer special tokens list (bos/eos).

alex: I'll spin a short quant run with mixed int8-fp32 option and compare the formatting tests (10-shot). Will post numbers in ~30m.

lia: Eval-bot reported initial pass: 92/100 preserved JSON structure, 6 had trailing garbage, 2 malformed. Uploading per-sample outputs to /internal/ai/evals/9876.

sophia: Thanks all. Triage decisions: blocking = stop/eos not respected in structured outputs; medium = minor streaming duplicates; low = perf tuning. Assignments: kevin -> tokenizer/eos mapping + batching settings; alex -> quant profile + perf/format tradeoff matrix; lia -> run full 1k eval if fixes land. I'll update the intake doc and add a short rollback trigger if we see >5% structured-output regressions in staging. :thumbsup:

matt: One more note — reproduction steps for the structured case are in the staging logs under job 1849505432: commands, payloads, raw outputs attached. Happy to pair with whoever debugs.

sophia: Great. If anyone hits a hard blocker, escalate in #incidents. Otherwise I'll check back in after alex/kevin updates. :sparkles:
